mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the FEDFUNDS rate above the 10-week moving average predicts a near-term negative S&P 500 20-day forward return due to tightened policy expectations.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above its 10-week moving average
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from the pre-tightening period (p > 0.05) during the identified trigger window.

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE falls below 4% for two consecutive months, labor market slack increases, boosting investor confidence and driving positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns show no statistically significant improvement over the prior 60-day average during the trigger period.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive monthly increases in HOUST (retail sales) of at least 3% above the prior month's level are associated with a positive S&P 20-day forward return as it signals resilient consumer demand.
candidate_trigger: HOUST monthly growth ≥ 3% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative or flat despite qualifying HOUST momentum in the trigger window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in INDPRO (industrial production) by more than 5% from the prior quarter is followed by a negative S&P 20-day forward return as it signals supply-side weakness.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive or at least equal to the prior quarter's average during the INDPRO shock.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS remains below 2% for three consecutive months, the persistence of ultra-loose policy is associated with a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return via equity risk premium expansion.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns show no outperformance versus the 60-day average during the accommodation period.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in PAYEMS (employment) by 10,000 or more in a month coincides with a negative S&P 500 5-day forward return due to market uncertainty about labor market stability.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not statistically negative during the trigger event (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous monthly increases in both GDPC1 (GDP) and RSAFS (retail sales) above their 12-month averages predict a positive S&P 20-day forward return as dual demand signals strengthen.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during the co-movement window (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE rises above 6% for two consecutive months in a contractionary regime, the S&P 20-day forward return turns negative as higher labor costs suppress corporate profits.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 6% for two consecutive months and macro regime is contractionary
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive during the UNRATE spike in a contractionary regime.
